shortDefinition: Keeping some of your money for later instead of spending it all right now. Like planting seeds that grow into future opportunities.
A plan for where your money goes, like giving every dollar a job. It helps you spend on needs first, then wants, while still saving for the future.
Costs that stay the same each month, like rent, phone bills, or insurance. These are predictable expenses you can plan for.
Costs that change from month to month, like groceries, gas, or entertainment. You have more control over these expenses.
Planting money seeds that can grow into more money over time. Instead of your money sitting still, it works for you by growing and multiplying.
When your money grows, and then the growth grows too! It's like planting a seed that becomes a tree, and that tree drops more seeds.
Not putting all your money in one place. Like a smart gardener plants different types of seeds in different spots, so if one fails, others keep growing.
Something useful or beneficial you provide to others. When you create value by solving problems or helping people, they're willing to pay you for it.
Money saved specifically for unexpected problems, like when your bike breaks or you need something urgently. It's your financial safety net.
Sharing your money, time, or skills to help others or support causes you believe in. It's about using your resources to make the world better.
Needs are things you must have to be safe and healthy (food, shelter, clothes). Wants are things that would be nice to have but aren't necessary.
Someone who starts their own business or finds creative ways to earn money by solving problems for others. They turn ideas into income.
A simple budgeting guideline: spend 50% on needs, 30% on wants, and save 20%. It helps you balance enjoying money today while building for tomorrow.
Regular money given by parents or guardians, often in exchange for chores or just for being part of the family. It's a great way to practice money skills.
All the money you receive, whether from allowance, gifts, jobs, or other sources. It's the money flowing into your life.
Money you spend on things. Every time you buy something or pay for a service, that's an expense - money flowing out of your life.
Extra money you earn for saving (or pay for borrowing). When you save money in a bank, they pay you interest for letting them use your money.
A safe place to keep your money at a bank. The bank protects your money and often pays you interest for keeping it there.
Something specific you want to achieve with your money, like saving $50 for a new game or $500 for a bike. Goals give your money a purpose.
Money you owe to someone else. If you borrow money, you have debt until you pay it back, usually with extra money called interest.
The ability to borrow money based on trust that you'll pay it back. Good credit means people trust you with money; bad credit means they don't.
Protection you pay for that helps cover big, unexpected costs. Like a safety net - if something bad happens, insurance helps pay for it.
The chance that something might not go as planned with your money. Higher risk investments might make more money but could also lose more.
Money you make after subtracting all your costs. If you sell lemonade for $10 but only spent $3 on supplies, your profit is $7.
When you end up with less money than you started with, either from a bad investment or spending more than you earn.
A dishonest trick designed to steal your money or personal information. If something sounds too good to be true, it probably is.
Thinking ahead about your money - setting goals, making budgets, and preparing for the future. Like making a roadmap for your financial journey.
What you give up when you choose one thing over another. If you spend $10 on candy, the opportunity cost is the book you could have bought instead.
Understanding how money works and how to manage it wisely. It's like learning to read, but for money - a skill that helps you throughout life.
When things gradually become more expensive over time. A candy bar that costs $1 today might cost $1.50 in the future due to inflation.
